use std::{error::Error, io, sync::Arc, time::Duration};

use axum::{
    body::to_bytes,
    extract::{Request, State},
    http::{header, HeaderMap, HeaderValue, Method, StatusCode},
    response::{IntoResponse, Response},
    Json, Router,
};
use hyper_util::{
    rt::{TokioIo, TokioTimer},
    service::TowerToHyperService,
};
use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
use tokio::{net::TcpListener, sync::Mutex, time::Instant};

use crate::sessions::{wire::MAX_SESSION_CONNECTIONS, SessionService};
use crate::{Runtime, MAX_FRAME_BYTES};
#[path = "session_ws.rs"]
mod session_ws;

pub const FRONTEND_ORIGIN: &str = "http://127.0.0.1:1420";
// Vite serves the same development frontend whether it is opened as 127.0.0.1
// or localhost, so a browser there sends either spelling as its Origin.
pub const FRONTEND_ORIGIN_LOCALHOST: &str = "http://localhost:1420";
pub const BACKEND_PORT: u16 = 1421;
const REQUEST_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);

#[cfg(feature = "bundled-frontend")]
include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/frontend.rs"));

struct HttpState {
    host: String,
    origin: String,
    credential: Vec<u8>,
    // Browser tabs share this runtime; it is the workspace writer.
    runtime: Arc<Mutex<Runtime>>,
    sessions: Arc<SessionService>,
    session_connections: Arc<tokio::sync::Semaphore>,
}

// Reject duplicate security headers instead of trusting whichever value is first.
fn single_header<'a>(headers: &'a HeaderMap, name: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
    let mut values = headers.get_all(name).iter();
    let value = values.next()?;
    if values.next().is_some() {
        return None;
    }
    value.to_str().ok()
}

fn reject(status: StatusCode, message: &'static str) -> Response {
    (status, message).into_response()
}

async fn dispatch(State(state): State<Arc<HttpState>>, request: Request) -> Response {
    let origin = single_header(request.headers(), "origin");
    let local_host = single_header(request.headers(), "host") == Some(state.host.as_str());
    let local_origin = origin.is_some_and(|origin| {
        origin == FRONTEND_ORIGIN || origin == FRONTEND_ORIGIN_LOCALHOST || origin == state.origin
    });
    let cors_origin = if local_host && local_origin {
        request.headers().get(header::ORIGIN).cloned()
    } else {
        None
    };
    let mut response = if !local_host {
        reject(StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "Use the local Agentica frontend.")
    } else if request.uri().path() != "/rpc"
        && (local_origin || !request.headers().contains_key("origin"))
    {
        serve_frontend(request)
    } else if local_origin {
        dispatch_local(state, request).await
    } else {
        reject(StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "Use the local Agentica frontend.")
    };
    let headers = response.headers_mut();
    headers.insert(header::CACHE_CONTROL, HeaderValue::from_static("no-store"));
    headers.insert(
        header::X_CONTENT_TYPE_OPTIONS,
        HeaderValue::from_static("nosniff"),
    );
    headers.insert(
        header::REFERRER_POLICY,
        HeaderValue::from_static("no-referrer"),
    );
    headers.insert(header::CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY, HeaderValue::from_static(
                    "default-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' ws://127.0.0.1:1421 https: http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:*; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'",
    ));
    if let Some(origin) = cors_origin {
        headers.insert(header::ACCESS_CONTROL_ALLOW_ORIGIN, origin);
        headers.insert(header::VARY, HeaderValue::from_static("Origin"));
    }
    response
}

fn serve_frontend(request: Request) -> Response {
    #[cfg(feature = "bundled-frontend")]
    if let Some((mime, bytes)) = request
        .uri()
        .path_and_query()
        .and_then(|path| frontend_asset(path.as_str()))
    {
        if !matches!(*request.method(), Method::GET | Method::HEAD) {
            let mut response = reject(StatusCode::METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, "Use GET or HEAD.");
            response
                .headers_mut()
                .insert(header::ALLOW, HeaderValue::from_static("GET, HEAD"));
            return response;
        }
        let body = if request.method() == Method::HEAD {
            &[][..]
        } else {
            bytes
        };
        let mut response = ([(header::CONTENT_TYPE, mime)], body).into_response();
        response
            .headers_mut()
            .insert(header::CONTENT_LENGTH, HeaderValue::from(bytes.len()));

  import { Handle, NodeResizer, Position } from "@xyflow/svelte";

      editable?: boolean;
      onEdit?: (text: string) => void;
      onResize?: (width: number, height: number) => void;
      onRetry?: () => void;
      onRead?: () => void;
    };
  }
  let { data, selected = false }: Props = $props();
  let editing = $state(false);
  let textarea = $state<HTMLTextAreaElement>();
  let body = $state<HTMLElement>();
  let overflowing = $state(false);

  const kind = $derived(
    data.role === "You"
      ? "prompt"
      : data.role === "Agent"
        ? "reply"
        : data.purpose === "instruction"
          ? "instruction"
          : "text",
  );
  const label = $derived(
    kind === "prompt"
      ? "You"
      : kind === "reply"
        ? "Agent"
        : kind === "instruction"
          ? "Instruction note"
          : "Text",
  );
  const turnState = $derived(data.role && turnStatus(data.status, data.role));
  const framed = $derived(kind !== "text" || !!data.preview);

  function edit() {
    if (!data.editable || data.preview) return;
    editing = true;
    requestAnimationFrame(() => textarea?.focus());
  }

  // Overflow is measured from layout boxes, which canvas zoom does not
  // change; detection never alters the node's saved or proposed geometry.
  $effect(() => {
    const element = body;
    void data.text;
    if (!element) return;
    const check = () => {
      overflowing = element.scrollHeight > element.clientHeight + 1;
    };
    const frame = requestAnimationFrame(check);
    const observer = new ResizeObserver(check);
    observer.observe(element);
    return () => {
      cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
      observer.disconnect();
    };
  });

# Changelog

Meaningful changes and development progress for Agentica. All entries below are
unreleased; this initial record includes committed history and current
working-tree changes. Dates identify development updates, not published releases.

Add completed changes under `Unreleased`; at release time, move them under the
released version and date. Keep validation evidence in the
[development docs](docs/development/README.md).

## Unreleased

### 2026-10-21

#### Let the canvas agent propose real HTML designs

- Add an `html` artifact type and a `createHtml` canvas operation. A design is a
  self-contained HTML/CSS page stored with the workspace and rendered on the
  canvas in a sandboxed frame without script execution; the app CSP blocks
  remote images, fonts, forms, and navigation. Designs can be moved, resized,
  reviewed, and reopened like other canvas objects.
- Ask for a screen or page and the agent proposes the design instead of
  describing it or sketching boxes. Designs are capped at 8,000 characters so
  one proposal plus its reply fits a runtime request frame; **Read HTML source**
  shows the exact source from the inspector.
- Upgrade workspace storage to version 6, rebuilding the artifact table to
  accept the new type while preserving every existing row.

#### Bound the canvas agent behind an explicit harness

- Extract the canvas agent loop from the OpenRouter adapter into
  `apps/desktop/src/lib/canvas-harness.ts`. A provider now only translates one
  request into a completion, so adding a provider cannot bypass a limit.
- Enforce per turn: eight provider requests, 32 tool calls, at most 16 calls per
  response, one `canvas_edit` tool, unique call IDs, 16 KiB arguments, 10,000
  character replies, a 90-second per-request deadline, and caller cancellation.
  Malformed calls end the turn; rejected calls return bounded feedback for
  repair; the third identical rejected edit ends the turn.
- Add named OpenAI-compatible provider presets for NVIDIA NIM, Groq, Together
  AI, Mistral AI, and DeepSeek. Each keeps its own base URL, API key, model, and
  tools flag, so switching endpoints cannot send one provider's key to another;
  the custom endpoint remains available for anything else.
- Replace the retired NVIDIA example model with a current catalog entry after
  the preset pointed users at a model that returns HTTP 410.
- Add **Test connection** in Settings. It sends one small message and reports
  latency, HTTP status, the provider's error detail, or a timeout, so retired
  models and unreachable endpoints no longer wait for the turn deadline.
- Raise the provider prompt cap to a separate 256 KiB limit. The old 16 KiB
  runtime-frame limit included a ~3 KiB tool schema and rejected ordinary
  canvases and history before any request was sent; runtime RPC stays at 16 KiB.
- Apply the same 256 KiB budget to a prompt's canvas snapshot in the runtime.
  A canvas with a few notes or drawings exceeded one 16 KiB frame, so
  `conversation.start` rejected every prompt with "Canvas context exceeds
  16 KiB" and the editor showed a save-recovery banner; the context check now
  uses the prompt budget and reports the measured size when it rejects.
- Raise the default per-request agent deadline from 90 to 180 seconds and make
  it configurable in Settings (30–600 seconds), so slow free models are not cut
  off mid-generation. The timeout error now points to the setting.
- Show live harness progress in the composer while a turn generates: the
  current request, staged edit count, and rejected calls. It updates from harness
  events and clears when the turn ends or is cancelled.
- Add `tests/agent-harness.test.mjs` covering each guard rail against a fake
  provider. Existing canvas tool, provider, and request-limit tests still pass.

### 2026-10-19

- Move session attention out of the canvas zoom controls into a top-bar
  "N waiting" queue (Ctrl+J / ⌘J). It lists every waiting session oldest first
  with waited time, **Jump to**, and **Mark seen**, so attention can be triaged
  at once instead of from a popover next to zoom. Tiles show an amber ring and a
  reason strip with the same **Mark seen** (sequence-aware `clearAttention`).
  Labels read "Waiting for you", "Stopped (exit code N)", and "Failed to start".
- Replace the project group's header card with a label cut into the group
  border, a ⋯ menu for Remove project and Locate folder, and separate status
  items built from structured counts instead of a joined summary string.
  `PROJECT_HEADER` stays 96 so persisted geometry validation does not change.
- Recover interrupted OSC sequences without swallowing the next escape byte or
  bell. Show Codex notification setup directly in tiles, provide the API-key URL
  as copyable text in desktop Settings, and omit empty quotes from notification
  labels. Align the attention design with Escape/CSI bell handling.
- Show session attention in tile headers, collapsed projects, and canvas
  navigation, with Go and Dismiss controls. Scan BEL and OSC 9 in the backend so
  renderer disposal and browser refresh cannot lose signals; bounded latches
  coalesce signals and focus gates raising. Labels quote received notifications
  without inferring agent/task state. Document opt-in Codex notification setup.
- Preserve CSI state when reporting BEL, and keep BEL inside DCS, APC, PM, and
  SOS strings ignored until termination. Track OSC separately so its terminating
  BEL still ends the string without raising attention.
- Report BEL after ESC while preserving escape state, so an intervening bell
  cannot swallow a following OSC 9 notification.
- Clear displayed attention when focusing an exited terminal after its output
  subscription detaches, using sequence-aware dismissal to preserve newer signals.
- Move the pointer to browser smoke-test click targets before pressing, so
  headless Chrome updates hit-testing before dispatching input.

- Wait for affected terminal output to drain before removing saved workspaces,
  canvases, projects, or tiles. Stream reads and acknowledgements still need that
  metadata after process exit; deleting it early could block later subscriptions.

### 2026-10-18

#### Release exited terminal subscriptions

- Drain and acknowledge the final PTY output before detaching exited sessions.
  Reclaim completed subscriptions before attaching another tile, so retained
  terminal history cannot exhaust the browser connection's eight slots.

#### Add project groups with native shell and Codex tiles

- Open existing folders as movable, collapsible project groups (desktop folder
  picker, or a backend path in browser mode). Groups hold explicitly owned shell
  and Codex tiles with group-relative layout; folder opening and canvas restore
  never launch commands, and missing folders offer **Locate folder**.
- A backend-lifetime PTY supervisor runs outside the workspace database lock so
  terminal output cannot stall saves. Sessions are bound to saved tile ownership,
  launched directly as executable plus argv, limited by shared named budgets,
  and stopped with process-session cleanup. Desktop streams over Tauri channels;
  the detached backend uses an origin-checked WebSocket authenticated by the
  first message rather than a URL key.
- One controller per session, no input replay, and explicit history gaps keep

> _Reasoning_
> The architecture is monorepo with SQLite storage, 16 KiB RPC frame, canvas artifact types text/drawing/html. Adding file attachments properly requires:
> 
> 1. Protocol: new `file` artifact schema (name, mime, size, data hash / content), new RPC methods for upload (binary chunk?) that bypass 16 KiB JSON frame, storage schema v7 for blobs, frontend file drop UI and rendering (image, PDF, docx text extraction).
> 2. Agent support: read extracted text into context.
> 
> This is a lot, and I should scope it. Given the "important decisions" rule, ask the user 2-3 questions: (a) which types to support first, (b) how they should appear (preview vs. text extraction vs. attach to prompt), (c) size limits.
> 
> However, too much questioning can be annoying. The request is clear at a high level: canvas should support images, docx, PDFs as canvas nodes. I can propose the design and ask one scoping question with recommended defaults.
> 
> Let me think about a tractable implementation that fits the repo's architecture and passes checks:
> 
> Minimal viable: Add a "file" artifact type storing a file as a workspace-relative path? Files dropped from OS could be read via Tauri; in browser mode, read via File API and send bytes base64. But 16 KiB frame limit blocks large files. Options:
> - Add an upload endpoint in Rust HTTP server (multipart or raw bytes) with auth; Tauri command for desktop. That's security-sensitive and big.
> - Chunked upload over existing RPC: add methods `file.create` (metadata) + `file.append` (base64 chunk ≤ ~10KB) — dozens of round trips for a 1 MB image, but workable? For a 5 MB image, 500 requests. Bad but functional. Still needs schema changes.
> - Store file contents in IndexedDB/localStorage in the frontend? Not persisted with workspace, breaks cross-device/browser reopen, and agent can't read.
> - For docx/pdf, extract text client-side (needs libs) and store as text artifact (10k char limit). Image could be stored as a data URL in the artifact but frame limit 16 KiB and LIMITS.maxSize. Not viable for real images.
> 
> Alternative pragmatic approach: reference a local file path (like project groups do with roots). Drop a file → register its absolute path + metadata in artifact. Frontend loads it via custom protocol (Tauri asset protocol) with `convertFileSrc`. Backend can read the file from disk for agent context (text extraction? PDF/docx parsing in Rust needs crates). Browser mode wouldn't work but desktop is primary. However, the CSP `img-src 'self' data:` blocks asset:// unless added.
> 
> Given the size, this is a multi-hour feature spanning Rust, protocol, and Svelte. I should ask the user to confirm scope and approach before implementing. Let me ask a focused set of questions with recommended defaults.
> 
> Questions:
> 1. What should happen when a file lands on the canvas? Options: preview inline + agent can read text; preview only; attach as context for prompts only. Multi-select maybe.
> 2. Which file types first? Images (png/jpg/webp/gif/svg), PDF, Word (docx; .doc legacy?), plain text/md/csv? Multi-select.
> 3. Storage approach: copy into workspace (portable, needs an upload path that bypasses 16 KiB) vs. link to original file path (fast, desktop-only, breaks if moved). This is an important design decision.
> 
> Also maybe size limit.
> 
> But before asking, ensure I understand what's feasible. Let me check Tauri permissions/capabilities for dialog (they have plugin-dialog). Adding file drop: Tauri drag-drop events give paths; reading files with fs plugin requires permission. Browser mode: File API.
> 
> Let me check the capabilities.

#![cfg_attr(not(debug_assertions), windows_subsystem = "windows")]

use agentica_runtime::{
    default_data_root,
    sessions::{
        wire::{SessionCommand, SessionEvent, SessionRequest, MAX_CONNECTION_SUBSCRIPTIONS},
        SessionOwner, SessionService,
    },
    DesktopBackend, Runtime,
};
use std::{
    collections::HashMap,
    sync::{
        atomic::{AtomicU8, Ordering},
        Arc, Mutex,
    },
    time::{Duration, Instant},
};
use tauri::Manager;

type Lease = (String, SessionOwner, String);
struct BackendState {
    runtime: Arc<Mutex<DesktopBackend>>,
    sessions: Arc<SessionService>,
    attachments: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, Lease>>>,
}

/// Input, resize, acknowledgement, and detach must name an attachment this
/// window created for the same saved owner and session identity.
fn owns_attachment(
    attachments: &HashMap<String, Lease>,
    label: &str,
    owner: &SessionOwner,
    session: &str,
    attachment: &str,
) -> bool {
    attachments
        .get(attachment)
        .is_some_and(|(saved_label, saved_owner, saved_session)| {
            saved_label == label && saved_owner == owner && saved_session == session
        })
}

#[tauri::command]
async fn runtime_request(
    request: serde_json::Value,
    connect: bool,
    state: tauri::State<'_, BackendState>,
) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
    let backend = state.runtime.clone();
    let sessions = state.sessions.clone();
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
        let method = request["method"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
        let params = &request["params"];
        let _guard = sessions
            .guard_metadata(method, params)
            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
        let response = backend
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| "Backend state is unavailable.".to_owned())?
            .request(&request, connect)?;
        if response.get("error").is_none() {
            sessions
                .forget_removed(method, params)
                .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
        }
        Ok(response)
    })
    .await
    .map_err(|error| format!("Backend task failed: {error}"))?
}

#[tauri::command]
async fn session_request(
    request: serde_json::Value,
    window: tauri::WebviewWindow,
    state: tauri::State<'_, BackendState>,
) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
    if window.label() != "main" {
        return Err("Session access is limited to the local main window.".into());
    }
    let request =
        SessionRequest::parse(&serde_json::to_vec(&request).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?)
            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
    if matches!(request.command, SessionCommand::Subscribe { .. }) {
        return Err("Use the session streaming channel to subscribe.".into());
    }
    if let Some((owner, session, attachment)) = request.command.attachment() {
        let attachments = state
            .attachments
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| "Attachment state is unavailable.")?;
        if !owns_attachment(&attachments, window.label(), owner, session, attachment) {
            return Err("This attachment does not belong to this window.".into());
        }
    }
    let sessions = state.sessions.clone();
    let attachments = state.attachments.clone();
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
        let detached = match &request.command {
            SessionCommand::Detach { attachment_id, .. } => Some(attachment_id.clone()),
            _ => None,
        };
        let response = sessions
            .execute(request.command)
            .map_err(|error| error.to_string());
        if let Some(id) = detached {
            if let Ok(mut attachments) = attachments.lock() {
                attachments.remove(&id);
            }
        }
        response
    })
    .await
    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?
}

#[tauri::command]
async fn session_subscribe(
    request: serde_json::Value,
    on_event: tauri::ipc::Channel<SessionEvent>,
    window: tauri::WebviewWindow,
    state: tauri::State<'_, BackendState>,
) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
    if window.label() != "main" {
        return Err("Session access is limited to the local main window.".into());
    }
    let request =
        SessionRequest::parse(&serde_json::to_vec(&request).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?)
            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
    let SessionCommand::Subscribe {
        owner,
        session_id,
        after,
    } = request.command
    else {
        return Err("A subscription command is required.".into());
    };
    let sessions = state.sessions.clone();
    let attachments = state.attachments.clone();
    let label = window.label().to_owned();
    let (result, id) = tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking({
        let (sessions, attachments, owner, session_id) = (
            sessions.clone(),
            attachments.clone(),
            owner.clone(),
            session_id.clone(),
        );
        move || {
            let mut leases = attachments
                .lock()
                .map_err(|_| "Attachment state is unavailable.")?;
            if leases.len() >= MAX_CONNECTION_SUBSCRIPTIONS {
                return Err("Too many terminal subscriptions.".to_owned());
            }
            let result = sessions
                .execute(SessionCommand::Subscribe {
                    owner: owner.clone(),
                    session_id: session_id.clone(),
                    after,
                })
                .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
            let id = result["attachmentId"]
                .as_str()
                .ok_or("Missing attachment identity.")?
                .to_owned();
            leases.insert(id.clone(), (label, owner, session_id));
            Ok((result, id))
        }
    })
    .await
    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())??;
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {
        let mut last = String::new();
        let mut heartbeat = Instant::now();
        loop {
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
            let (service, own, session, attachment) = (
                sessions.clone(),
                owner.clone(),
                session_id.clone(),
                id.clone(),
            );
            let event = tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
                service.event(&own, &session, &attachment)
            })
            .await;
            let Ok(Ok(event)) = event else {
                break;
            };
            let status = serde_json::to_string(&event.status).unwrap_or_default();
            if event.output.frames.is_empty()
                && !event.output.history_gap
                && status == last
                && heartbeat.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(1)
            {
                continue;
            }
            if on_event.send(event).is_err() {
                break;
            }
            last = status;
            heartbeat = Instant::now();
        }
        sessions.release(&owner, &session_id, &id);
        if let Ok(mut attachments) = attachments.lock() {
            attachments.remove(&id);
        };
    });
    Ok(result)
}

#[tauri::command]
async fn session_shutdown(
    window: tauri::WebviewWindow,
    state: tauri::State<'_, BackendState>,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    if window.label() != "main" {
        return Err("Session access is limited to the local main window.".into());
    }
    let service = state.sessions.clone();
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
        service.shutdown().map_err(|error| error.to_string())
    })
    .await
    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?
}

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let root = default_data_root();
    let sessions = Arc::new(SessionService::new(root.clone()));
    let exiting = Arc::new(AtomicU8::new(0));
    tauri::Builder::default()
        .plugin(tauri_plugin_http::init())
        .plugin(tauri_plugin_dialog::init())
        .manage(BackendState {
            runtime: Arc::new(Mutex::new(DesktopBackend::new(Runtime::new(root)))),
            sessions: sessions.clone(),
            attachments: Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),
        })
        .invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![
            runtime_request,
            session_request,
            session_subscribe,
            session_shutdown
        ])
        .build(tauri::generate_context!())?
        .run(move |app, event| {
            if let tauri::RunEvent::ExitRequested { api, .. } = event {
                if exiting.load(Ordering::SeqCst) == 2 {
                    return;
                }
                api.prevent_exit();
                if exiting
                    .compare_exchange(0, 1, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst)
                    .is_ok()
                {
                    let (sessions, exiting, app) = (sessions.clone(), exiting.clone(), app.clone());
                    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
                        if sessions.shutdown().is_ok() {
                            exiting.store(2, Ordering::SeqCst);
                            app.exit(0);
                        } else {
                            exiting.store(0, Ordering::SeqCst);
                            if let Some(window) = app.get_webview_window("main") {
                                let _ = window.show();
                            }
                        }
                    });
                }
            }
        });
    Ok(())
}

    #[test]

        let tile = owner("00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003");
        let request = |command: serde_json::Value| {
            SessionRequest::parse(
                &serde_json::to_vec(&serde_json::json!({"id": "ipc", "command": command})).unwrap(),
            )
        };
        let reference = serde_json::json!({"owner": tile,
            "sessionId": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004",
            "attachmentId": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005"});
        let with = |extra: serde_json::Value| {
            let mut command = reference.clone();
            command
                .as_object_mut()
                .unwrap()
                .extend(extra.as_object().unwrap().clone());
            command
        };
        assert!(request(with(serde_json::json!({"op": "input", "bytes": [3]}))).is_ok());
        for invalid in [
            with(serde_json::json!({"op": "input", "bytes": vec![0_u8; 16385]})),
            with(serde_json::json!({"op": "resize", "rows": 0, "cols": 80})),
            with(serde_json::json!({"op": "acknowledge", "sequence": -1})),
            with(serde_json::json!({"op": "input", "bytes": [3], "extra": true})),
        ] {
            assert!(request(invalid).is_err());
        }
    }

mod commands;
pub mod contracts;
pub mod http;
pub mod sessions;
mod store;

use serde::Deserialize;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

pub use commands::Runtime;
pub use store::{default_data_root, RuntimeError, STORAGE_VERSION};

pub const MAX_FRAME_BYTES: usize = 16 * 1024;

/// Canvas context is prompt data, not a transport frame. A canvas can easily
/// hold more than one frame's worth of objects, so bound it by the provider
/// prompt budget instead (apps/desktop/src/lib/openrouter.ts).
pub const MAX_CANVAS_CONTEXT_BYTES: usize = 256 * 1024;

#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", deny_unknown_fields)]
struct Request {
    protocol_version: f64,
    id: String,
    method: String,
    params: Option<Value>,
}

const INVALID_REQUEST: &str =
    "Expected protocol version 1, an id, a supported method, and its params.";

fn error(id: Option<&str>, code: &str, message: &str) -> Value {
    json!({ "protocolVersion": 1, "id": id, "error": { "code": code, "message": message } })
}

impl Runtime {
    /// Validate and dispatch a versioned JSON request from either transport.
    /// Envelope errors have a null id; command errors are correlated.
    pub fn handle_request(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Value {
        if bytes.len() > MAX_FRAME_BYTES {
            return error(None, "FRAME_TOO_LARGE", "Requests must fit in 16 KiB.");
        }
        let input = match serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(bytes) {
            Ok(input) => input,
            Err(_) => return error(None, "INVALID_JSON", "Expected a JSON request."),
        };
        if !input.is_object() {
            return error(None, "INVALID_REQUEST", INVALID_REQUEST);
        }
        // `runtime.ping` takes no params, not even null.
        let has_params = input.get("params").is_some();
        let request = match serde_json::from_value::<Request>(input) {
            Ok(request)
                if request.protocol_version == 1.0
                    && !request.id.is_empty()
                    // Zod measures JavaScript strings in UTF-16 code units.
                    && request.id.encode_utf16().count() <= 128
                    && (if request.method == "runtime.ping" {
                        !has_params
                    } else {
                        commands::METHODS.contains(&request.method.as_str())
                    }) =>
            {
                request
            }
            _ => return error(None, "INVALID_REQUEST", INVALID_REQUEST),
        };
        if request.method == "runtime.ping" {
            return json!({ "protocolVersion": 1, "id": request.id, "result": { "status": "ok" } });
        }
        match self.call(&request.method, request.params.unwrap_or(Value::Null)) {
            Ok(result) => json!({ "protocolVersion": 1, "id": request.id, "result": result }),
            Err(failure) => error(Some(&request.id), failure.code, &failure.message),
        }
    }
}

/// Desktop connection state; the runtime is linked into the Tauri process.
pub struct DesktopBackend {
    connected: bool,
    runtime: Runtime,
}

impl DesktopBackend {
    pub fn new(runtime: Runtime) -> Self {
        Self {
            connected: false,
            runtime,
        }
    }

    pub fn request(&mut self, request: &Value, connect: bool) -> Result<Value, String> {
        let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(request).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
        if bytes.len() > MAX_FRAME_BYTES {
            return Err("Requests must fit in 16 KiB.".to_owned());
        }
        if connect {
            self.connected = true;
        }
        if !self.connected {
            return Err("Backend disconnected. Reconnect to start it.".to_owned());
        }
        Ok(self.runtime.handle_request(&bytes))
    }
}

-- Designs store their source in text_content; the artifact type tells the
-- canvas to render it in a sandboxed frame instead of as prose. SQLite cannot
-- change a CHECK constraint in place, so rebuild the table and copy every row.
CREATE TABLE artifact_v6 (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('text', 'drawing', 'html')),
    schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (schema_version = 1),
    revision INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (revision >= 1),
    content_store TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (content_store = 'sqlite'),
    content_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
) STRICT;

INSERT INTO artifact_v6 (id, type, schema_version, revision, content_store, content_id)
    SELECT id, type, schema_version, revision, content_store, content_id FROM artifact;

DROP TABLE artifact;
ALTER TABLE artifact_v6 RENAME TO artifact;

> _Reasoning_
> I now understand the architecture. This feature is substantial but doable with a reasonable scope:
> 
> Plan: Add file artifacts to the canvas:
> - New artifact type "file" (or distinct types image/pdf/docx?). Better one "file" artifact with `name`, `mime`, `size`, and content stored as binary/base64 in DB? SQLite blob storage.
> - Need upload bypassing 16 KiB frames. Add Tauri command `file_upload`? Or runtime method accepting base64 chunks? The 16 KiB cap is enforced at multiple layers (protocol request schema? no size limit; runtime handle_request). HTTP /rpc has body limit. Chunked upload via RPC: `file.create` metadata + repeated `file.append` with base64 chunk ~8KB. This works with both transports and existing auth, no new attack surface. For a 1 MB image ~170 requests — slow but acceptable? Hmm, 16KiB frame => chunk base64 ~10KB => 100 requests per MB. Could be a few seconds. Might be tolerable but ugly.
> 
> Alternative: Tauri-specific upload command reading from path directly on backend, plus browser-mode HTTP upload endpoint. But then artifact creation still needs RPC. Desktop primary, but browser dev mode used heavily (screenshot tests likely). Let me check tests to see how they drive the app (headless Chrome => browser mode with backend). If browser mode must work, upload needs HTTP endpoint anyway.
> 
> Hmm, maybe simpler: serve files from backend via HTTP GET with the runtime reading them from the filesystem path, and store only path + metadata in artifact. Drag & drop in Tauri gives file paths. Browser mode drag & drop can't give a real path; but in browser mode the user could pick a file via <input type=file> and then... no.
> 
> Let me check how tests run and what scope is expected. Also check `docs/development`.
> 
> Actually, before over-engineering, let me ask the user. They may be fine with a simpler feature set: e.g., "drop an image/PDF/DOCX on the canvas, it becomes a node you can preview; the agent can see extracted text". But decisions like storage/portability matter.
> 
> Given the instruction to ask about important decisions, I'll ask:
> 
> 1. Scope of files: images + PDF + Word docs only? or also text/markdown/csv/svg? 
> 2. Behavior: preview node + agent-readable text? 
> 3. Storage: copy into workspace (works in browser too, upload needed) vs. link to source path (desktop only).
>

# Agentica

A visual workspace operating system for your agents with infinite canvas

The repository currently contains an initial development scaffold: a Svelte canvas
shell, a Tauri desktop host with a shared Rust runtime, and a detached Axum
backend for the same UI in a local browser. Both modes support validated health
checks and visible connection failures. The shared runtime persists workspaces,
canvases, and text artifacts in SQLite with one writer per workspace; the UI
creates and reopens them, edits text and node placement, persists pan/zoom, and
autosaves changes through the runtime commands. OpenRouter conversations place
editable prompts and replies directly on the canvas. Tool-capable models can
propose text, shape, placement, and connection changes for review.

## Canvas conversation

Open Settings to choose OpenRouter, a named hosted provider (NVIDIA NIM, Groq,
Together AI, Mistral AI, or DeepSeek), or a custom OpenAI-compatible provider.
Named presets fill their hosted endpoint and keep a separate base URL, API key,
model, and tools flag, so switching providers cannot send one provider's key to
another. Custom providers accept any base URL (for example
`https://api.example.com/v1` or `http://localhost:1234/v1`), API key, and model
ID. Leave the key blank for endpoints that need no authentication. Enable canvas
tools only for models that support function calling; disable them for text-only
replies.OpenRouter checks its model
catalog automatically. **Test connection** sends one small message and reports
the endpoint's HTTP status, the model error, or a timeout, so misconfigured keys,
retired model IDs, and unreachable endpoints surface before a canvas turn. Each
provider keeps separate settings and keys locally.
The desktop app sends custom requests through its native HTTP client, so providers
do not need browser CORS support. Browser mode sends requests directly and requires
CORS from the app's origin. Custom URLs support HTTPS, or HTTP at `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`.
The app appends `/chat/completions` to the base URL; pasting the full Chat
Completions URL is also supported.

Select objects to focus
the next request, or clear the selection to use the current canvas. The composer
shows what will be sent: object text and geometry plus up to eight recent
exchanges. Text-only models can reply but cannot propose object changes.

Prompts and replies remain editable canvas text: double-click or focus the text
and press Enter to edit it. Escape or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter ends editing. Text and
geometric shapes can be moved and resized with selection controls.

Proposed changes use dashed outlines and a **Proposed** label. Choose **Apply**
beside the reply to commit the whole proposal, or **Discard** to keep the reply
without changing existing objects. Pending proposals survive reopening; changed
targets cause a conflict rather than overwriting manual edits. Only one generation
or unresolved proposal can be active on a canvas. Cancel stops generation, and
interrupted requests require an explicit retry.

The first tool set supports text, labeled rectangles and ellipses, placement,
connectors, and self-contained HTML/CSS designs. Ask for a screen (for example
“design a login page”) and the agent proposes a page rendered on the canvas in
a sandboxed frame: scripts, remote resources, and form submission are blocked,
and **Read HTML source** shows the exact source. Designs are stored with the
workspace, not written into a project folder. The agent does not generate images
or execute code. Provider prompts are
capped at 256 KiB, and a prompt's canvas snapshot shares that budget instead of
the 16 KiB runtime RPC frame limit; oversized requests fail visibly without
truncation and report the measured size. If saving a generated response fails, keep the canvas open to retry
or copy the response for recovery. Basic manual editing needs no AI account.

The canvas agent runs inside a fixed harness, so every provider shares the same
budgets. A turn allows at most eight provider requests and 32 tool calls (16 per
response) through the one `canvas_edit` tool. Malformed, duplicate, or oversized
calls end the turn; tool arguments are capped at 16 KiB, replies at 10,000
characters, and each request has a 180-second deadline, adjustable in Settings
between 30 and 600 seconds. A rejected edit is
returned to the model for correction, and the third identical rejected edit ends
the turn. Cancel aborts the in-flight request. Nothing is applied until **Apply**.
While a turn runs, the composer reports the current request (for example,
"Request 2 of 8"), how many edits are staged, and any rejected calls.

## Project groups and native sessions

Choose **Open project** to place an existing folder on the canvas as a project
group. The desktop app shows a folder picker; browser mode asks for an absolute
folder path on the backend computer. Opening a folder copies and creates nothing
and runs no command. Groups start collapsed on every canvas visit; the header
chevron expands one. Each group header offers **Add terminal** (your login shell,
or `/bin/sh` as a visible fallback) and **Add agent** (the installed Codex CLI with
its own sign-in, prompts, and approvals). Tiles belong to their group, move with it,
and start only when you choose **Start**. Sessions run with your user permissions;
the project folder sets the working directory and is not a sandbox.

Codex must be installed as `codex` on the PATH of the backend process (or the
desktop app). Agentica passes no prompt, approval, or sandbox flags and never
answers native prompts for you.

- **Focus terminal** sends keys, Ctrl+C, Tab, and Escape to the program.
  **Ctrl+Shift+Escape** returns focus to the tile controls; **Ctrl+Shift+C** copies
  the selection. Paste needs an explicit paste action, and multi-line pastes ask
  for confirmation. Links open only with Ctrl/Cmd+click in browser mode.
- Moving, resizing, collapsing a group, switching canvases, or refreshing the
  browser does not stop a session; returning reattaches without replaying input.
  If earlier output was dropped, the tile says so. **Redraw** asks the program to
  repaint its current screen; it does not recover lost history.
- Removing a tile, group, canvas, or workspace with live sessions asks you to
  **Stop and remove** or **Cancel**. Removal never deletes project files.
- Process ownership: closing the desktop window stops and reaps its sessions.
  In browser mode the backend owns them; closing a tab only detaches, and
  stopping the backend (Ctrl+C) stops them. After a restart, tiles reappear
  stopped. Deliberately daemonized processes and abrupt backend crashes are
  outside this cleanup.
- If a project folder moves, Start is disabled and **Locate folder** rebinds the
  group once its sessions are stopped.

Native sessions are supported on Linux only, verified with zsh 5.9 and
`codex-cli 0.163.0` in desktop and browser modes. On other systems project groups remain
visible but Start explains why it is unavailable. Project paths, session
settings, and terminal output are never added to canvas conversation context.

## Getting started

Run all commands from the repository root.

| What you want to run                     | Prerequisites                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frontend development or built-UI preview | Node.js 24 and pnpm 11.6.0                                                                              |
===
| Frontend development or built-UI preview | Node.js 24 and pnpm 11.6.0                                                                              |
| Build the detached distribution          | Frontend tools, stable Rust and Cargo; desktop libraries are not needed                                 |
| Desktop development or builds            | Frontend tools, Rust, and the [Tauri platform prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/) |
| An already compiled backend              | No Node, pnpm, or Rust toolchain required                                                               |
| An already compiled desktop app          | Platform runtime libraries/webview; no Node, pnpm, or Rust toolchain required                           |

Install JavaScript dependencies before using the frontend or desktop commands:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

## Session attention

Session tiles show attention for terminal bells (BEL), program-declared OSC 9
notifications, and an unseen process exit or launch failure. An affected tile gets
an amber ring (red for a failed launch) and a strip under the terminal with the
reason, how long it has waited, and **Mark seen**. Project groups list separate
status items, such as "1 running" and "2 waiting for you", also when collapsed.

The top bar shows how many sessions on the current canvas are waiting. Select it,
or press Ctrl+J (⌘J on macOS) outside text fields and terminals, to open the
queue: every waiting session, oldest first, with its project, reason, and waited
time. Up and Down move between rows, Enter jumps to the tile, and Escape closes
the queue. **Jump to** moves the viewport without expanding a collapsed project or
clearing attention. Focus the terminal or choose **Mark seen** to clear it.

Labels describe only received signals: **Waiting for you** for a terminal bell,
the program's notification text (or **Sent a notification** when it is empty),
**Stopped** with the exit code or signal, and **Failed** with the error (or
**Failed to start**). They do not establish approval, thinking, turn completion,
or task results. Title, directory, and progress escape sequences do not raise
attention.

Attention remains in the backend across canvas switches and browser refreshes;
it resets when the session is restarted or the backend ends. Signals while the
terminal is focused, and user-requested Stop/Restart/removal exits, do not raise
attention. Notification text stays out of saved canvas content and conversations.

Codex tiles include expandable notification setup instructions. To opt in, add
these settings to your Codex configuration:

```toml
[tui]
notifications = true
notification_method = "osc9"
notification_condition = "always"
```

These are global Codex settings (normally `~/.codex/config.toml`) and also affect
Codex in other terminals, including notifications while focused there. `osc9`
avoids relying on inherited terminal detection; `always` lets Agentica apply its
own terminal-focus gating. Agentica does not inspect or modify Codex configuration
or add launch flags. Without this opt-in, bell and process-exit attention still
work; the setup hint does not indicate whether Codex is configured.

## Running the application

| Option                                                              | How to start                                                 | What opens                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| [Desktop development](#desktop-development)                         | `pnpm dev`                                                   | Tauri window with the shared Rust runtime             |
| [Compiled desktop app](#compiled-desktop-app)                       | `pnpm build:desktop`, then run the executable                | Tauri window with the built frontend and Rust runtime |
| [Browser development](#browser-development)                         | `pnpm dev:backend` and `pnpm dev:web` in separate terminals  | Browser UI connected to an independent Axum backend   |
| [Browser with a compiled backend](#browser-with-a-compiled-backend) | `pnpm build:backend`, then run the executable                | Embedded browser UI and Rust runtime on port 1421     |
| [Preview the built browser UI](#preview-the-built-browser-ui)       | Run a backend and serve the built frontend with Vite preview | Local preview of the built UI                         |
| [Frontend only](#frontend-only)                                     | `pnpm dev:web`                                               | Canvas UI without a connected backend                 |

The UI implements canvas display, runtime health checks, workspace and canvas
creation and reopening, text and node placement editing, persisted pan/zoom,
and debounced autosave with recovery when saves fail. None of these options
requires Codex or an AI account. Workspaces are stored in `AGENTICA_DATA_DIR`
when set, otherwise in the OS data directory (`~/.local/share/agentica` on Linux,
`%APPDATA%\agentica` on Windows); both launch modes share it.

### Desktop development

```sh
pnpm dev
```

This builds the protocol package, starts Vite, compiles the desktop app, and opens
a Tauri window. The app calls its linked Rust runtime through Tauri commands and
connects automatically. A separate backend terminal is not needed. Closing the
window ends its backend; stop the development command with Ctrl+C when finished.

### Compiled desktop app

Build the release app with its frontend embedded:

```sh
pnpm build:desktop
```

Then launch it on your platform:

| Platform           | Command                                 |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| Linux              | `./target/release/agentica-desktop`     |
| Windows PowerShell | `.\target\release\agentica-desktop.exe` |

The executable includes the Rust runtime. No Vite server or separate backend is
needed. Closing the app ends the runtime. This command builds an executable;
installer generation remains pending.

### Browser development

Terminal 1 — backend:

```sh
pnpm dev:backend
```

Terminal 2 — frontend:

```sh
pnpm dev:web
```

The backend command compiles and starts the Rust/Axum server. It is a convenience
alias for this direct Cargo command, which needs no Node or pnpm:

```sh
cargo run --locked -p agentica-runtime --bin agentica-backend
```

Follow [the browser connection steps](#browser-connection-and-shutdown) below.

### Browser with a compiled backend

Build the release distribution (frontend tooling is required at build time):

```sh
pnpm build:backend
```

Copy `target/release/agentica-backend` (Windows: `.exe`) to the destination and
run it. It embeds the built UI; open `http://127.0.0.1:1421`, paste the terminal
key, and select **Connect**. No Vite, asset directory, Node, pnpm, or Cargo is
needed at runtime. Linux still requires compatible glibc, libgcc, and libm;
use a local browser.

async fn dispatch_local(state: Arc<HttpState>, request: Request) -> Response {
    let deadline = Instant::now() + REQUEST_TIMEOUT;
    if request.uri().path_and_query().map(|path| path.as_str()) != Some("/rpc") {
        return reject(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "Unknown endpoint.");
    }
    if request.method() == Method::OPTIONS {
        let headers = request.headers();
        let requested_headers =
            single_header(headers, "access-control-request-headers").unwrap_or("");
        if single_header(headers, "access-control-request-method") != Some("POST")
            || headers
                .get_all("access-control-request-headers")
                .iter()
                .count()
                > 1
            || (!requested_headers.is_empty()
                && requested_headers.split(',').any(|name| {
                    !matches!(
                        name.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str(),
                        "authorization" | "content-type"
                    )
                }))
        {
            return reject(StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "Unsupported preflight.");
        }
        let mut response = StatusCode::NO_CONTENT.into_response();
        response.headers_mut().insert(
            header::ACCESS_CONTROL_ALLOW_METHODS,
            HeaderValue::from_static("POST"),
        );
        response.headers_mut().insert(
            header::ACCESS_CONTROL_ALLOW_HEADERS,
            HeaderValue::from_static("Authorization, Content-Type"),
        );
        return response;
    }
    let supplied = single_header(request.headers(), "authorization")
        .unwrap_or("")
        .as_bytes();
    if !bool::from(state.credential.as_slice().ct_eq(supplied)) {
        return reject(
            StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
            "Invalid connection key. Copy the current key from the backend terminal.",
        );
    }
    if request.method() != Method::POST {
        let mut response = reject(StatusCode::METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, "Use POST.");
        response
            .headers_mut()
            .insert(header::ALLOW, HeaderValue::from_static("POST, OPTIONS"));
        return response;
    }
    if single_header(request.headers(), "content-type") != Some("application/json") {
        return reject(StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "Use application/json.");
    }
    let bytes =
        match tokio::time::timeout_at(deadline, to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_FRAME_BYTES))
            .await
        {
            Ok(Ok(bytes)) => bytes,
            Ok(Err(error))
                if error
                    .source()
                    .is_some_and(|source| source.is::<http_body_util::LengthLimitError>()) =>
            {
                return reject(
                    StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE,
                    "Requests must fit in 16 KiB.",
                );
            }
            Ok(Err(_)) => return reject(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "Cannot read request body."),
            Err(_) => return reject(StatusCode::REQUEST_TIMEOUT, "Request timed out."),
        };
    let mut runtime =
        match tokio::time::timeout_at(deadline, state.runtime.clone().lock_owned()).await {
            Ok(runtime) => runtime,
            Err(_) => {
                return reject(
                    StatusCode::REQUEST_TIMEOUT,
                    "Request timed out before execution. Nothing was saved.",
                );
            }
        };
    // A started blocking mutation cannot be cancelled; await its committed outcome.
    let sessions = state.sessions.clone();
    match tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
        let request: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).unwrap_or_default();
        let method = request["method"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
        let params = &request["params"];
        match sessions.guard_metadata(method, params) {
            Ok(_guard) => {
                let response = runtime.handle_request(&bytes);
                if response.get("error").is_none() { let _ = sessions.forget_removed(method, params); }
                response
            }
            Err(error) => serde_json::json!({"protocolVersion": 1, "id": request["id"], "error": {"code": error.code, "message": error.message}}),
        }
    }).await {
        Ok(reply) => Json(reply).into_response(),
        Err(_) => reject(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "Backend runtime failed."),
    }
}

/// Serve authenticated loopback RPC and optional embedded UI with HTTP deadlines.
pub async fn serve(
    listener: TcpListener,
    connection_key: &str,
    runtime: Runtime,
) -> io::Result<()> {
    let sessions = Arc::new(SessionService::new(
        runtime.data_root().map(std::path::Path::to_owned),
    ));
    serve_with_sessions(listener, connection_key, runtime, sessions).await
}

pub async fn serve_with_sessions(
    listener: TcpListener,
    connection_key: &str,
    runtime: Runtime,
    sessions: Arc<SessionService>,
) -> io::Result<()> {
    if !listener.local_addr()?.ip().is_loopback() {
        return Err(io::Error::other("The backend must bind to loopback."));
    }
    let app = Router::new()
        .route("/sessions", session_ws::route())
        .fallback(dispatch)
        .with_state(Arc::new(HttpState {
            host: format!("127.0.0.1:{}", listener.local_addr()?.port()),
            origin: format!("http://127.0.0.1:{}", listener.local_addr()?.port()),
            credential: format!("Bearer {connection_key}").into_bytes(),
            runtime: Arc::new(Mutex::new(runtime)),
            sessions,
            session_connections: Arc::new(tokio::sync::Semaphore::new(MAX_SESSION_CONNECTIONS)),
        }));
    loop {
        let (stream, _) = listener.accept().await?;
        let service = TowerToHyperService::new(app.clone());
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            // Axum's default serve helper does not expose the header deadline.
            let mut http = hyper::server::conn::http1::Builder::new();
            http.timer(TokioTimer::new())
                .header_read_timeout(REQUEST_TIMEOUT)
                .max_buf_size(MAX_FRAME_BYTES);
            // Peer disconnects and malformed HTTP are ordinary connection errors.
            let _ = http
                .serve_connection(TokioIo::new(stream), service)
                .with_upgrades()
                .await;
        });
    }
}

const MAX_TEXT: usize = 10_000;
/// A design travels in one proposal operation, so it must leave room for the
/// reply inside a single request frame.
const MAX_HTML: usize = 8_000;
const MAX_COORDINATE: f64 = 1_000_000.0;
const MIN_SIZE: f64 = 40.0;
const MAX_SIZE: f64 = 4_000.0;
const MIN_ZOOM: f64 = 0.1;
const MAX_ZOOM: f64 = 4.0;

const MAX_REVISION: u64 = (1 << 53) - 1;
const TEXT_SCHEMA_VERSION: i64 = 1;
const DRAWING_SCHEMA_VERSION: i64 = 1;
const MAX_SHAPES: usize = 1_000;
const MAX_POINTS: usize = 10_000;
const MAX_STROKE_WIDTH: f64 = 64.0;

];

pub(crate) fn invalid(message: impl Into<String>) -> RuntimeError {
    RuntimeError::new("INVALID_PARAMS", message)
}

fn not_found(what: &str) -> RuntimeError {
    RuntimeError::new("NOT_FOUND", format!("{what} not found in this workspace."))
}

fn conflict(what: &str, revision: i64) -> RuntimeError {
    RuntimeError::new(
        "CONFLICT",
        format!("The {what} changed since it was loaded (now revision {revision}). Reload it, then retry."),
    )
}

fn parse<T: DeserializeOwned>(params: Value) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
    if !params.is_object() {
        return Err(invalid("Parameters must be a JSON object."));
    }
    serde_json::from_value(params).map_err(|error| invalid(format!("Invalid parameters: {error}.")))
}

pub(crate) fn id(field: &str, value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if is_id(value) {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(invalid(format!("{field} must be a lowercase UUID.")))
    }
}

// Zod measures JavaScript strings in UTF-16 code units.
pub(crate) fn label(field: &str, value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    // Match JavaScript trim(), whose whitespace set differs from Rust's.
    let blank = value.chars().all(|c| {
        matches!(
            c,
            '\u{0009}'..='\u{000d}'
                | '\u{0020}'
                | '\u{00a0}'
                | '\u{1680}'
                | '\u{2000}'..='\u{200a}'
                | '\u{2028}'
                | '\u{2029}'
                | '\u{202f}'
                | '\u{205f}'
                | '\u{3000}'
                | '\u{feff}'
        )
    });
    if blank || value.encode_utf16().count() > MAX_LABEL {
        return Err(invalid(format!(
            "{field} must contain 1 to {MAX_LABEL} characters."
        )));
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(crate) fn text(value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if value.encode_utf16().count() > MAX_TEXT {
        return Err(invalid(format!(
            "text must not exceed {MAX_TEXT} characters."
        )));
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(crate) fn html(value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if value.trim().is_empty() {
        return Err(invalid("A design must contain HTML."));
    }
    if value.encode_utf16().count() > MAX_HTML {
        return Err(invalid(format!(
            "A design must not exceed {MAX_HTML} characters."
        )));

fn save_text(
    tx: &Transaction,
    artifact_id: &str,
    expected: i64,
    body: &str,
) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError> {
    let current: Option<(String, i64)> = tx
        .query_row(
            "SELECT type, revision FROM artifact WHERE id = ?1",
            [artifact_id],
            |row| Ok((row.get(0)?, row.get(1)?)),
        )
        .optional()?;
    match current {
        None => return Err(not_found("Artifact")),
        Some((kind, _)) if kind != "text" => return Err(not_found("Text artifact")),
        Some((_, current)) if current != expected => return Err(conflict("artifact", current)),
        Some(_) => {}
    }
    tx.execute(
        "UPDATE text_content SET body = ?2
         WHERE id = (SELECT content_id FROM artifact WHERE id = ?1)",
        (artifact_id, body),
    )?;
    tx.execute(
        "UPDATE artifact SET revision = revision + 1 WHERE id = ?1",
        [artifact_id],
    )?;
    artifact(tx, artifact_id)
}

fn artifact(tx: &Transaction, artifact_id: &str) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError> {
    let (kind, schema_version, revision, content_id): (String, i64, i64, String) = tx
        .query_row(
            "SELECT type, schema_version, revision, content_id FROM artifact WHERE id = ?1",
            [artifact_id],
            |row| Ok((row.get(0)?, row.get(1)?, row.get(2)?, row.get(3)?)),
        )
        .optional()?
        .ok_or_else(|| not_found("Artifact"))?;
    match kind.as_str() {
        "text" => {
            let (body, purpose): (String, String) = tx.query_row(
                "SELECT body, purpose FROM text_content WHERE id = ?1",
                [&content_id],
                |row| Ok((row.get(0)?, row.get(1)?)),
            )?;
            Ok(json!({
                "id": artifact_id, "type": "text",
                "schemaVersion": schema_version,
                "revision": revision,
                "text": body, "purpose": purpose,
            }))
        }
        // Designs share the text store but keep their own artifact type so the
        // canvas renders them in a sandboxed frame instead of as prose.
        "html" => {
            let body: String = tx.query_row(
                "SELECT body FROM text_content WHERE id = ?1",
                [&content_id],
                |row| row.get(0),
            )?;
            Ok(json!({
                "id": artifact_id, "type": "html",
                "schemaVersion": schema_version,
                "revision": revision,
                "html": body,
            }))
        }
        "drawing" => {
            let body: String = tx.query_row(
                "SELECT body FROM drawing_content WHERE id = ?1",
                [&content_id],
                |row| row.get(0),
            )?;
            let drawing: Value = serde_json::from_str(&body).map_err(|error| {
                RuntimeError::new(
                    "STORAGE_ERROR",
                    format!("A stored drawing is unreadable: {error}."),
                )
            })?;
            Ok(json!({
                "id": artifact_id, "type": "drawing",
                "schemaVersion": schema_version,
                "revision": revision,
                "drawing": drawing,
            }))
        }
        _ => Err(RuntimeError::new(
            "STORAGE_ERROR",
            "A stored artifact has an unknown type.",
        )),
    }
}

fn canvas_state(tx: &Transaction, canvas_id: &str) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError> {
    let canvas = tx
        .query_row(
            "SELECT title, revision, viewport_x, viewport_y, viewport_zoom FROM canvas WHERE id = ?1",
            [canvas_id],
            |row| {
                Ok(json!({
                    "id": canvas_id,
                    "title": row.get::<_, String>(0)?,
                    "revision": row.get::<_, i64>(1)?,
                    "viewport": {
                        "x": row.get::<_, f64>(2)?,
                        "y": row.get::<_, f64>(3)?,
                        "zoom": row.get::<_, f64>(4)?,
                    },
                }))
            },
        )
        .optional()?
        .ok_or_else(|| not_found("Canvas"))?;
    let mut statement = tx.prepare(
        "SELECT id, artifact_id, x, y, width, height FROM canvas_node
         WHERE canvas_id = ?1 ORDER BY rowid",

> _Reasoning_
> Implementation is possible but large. I need to be efficient. Let's define a concrete plan that I can execute reliably, and keep Rust changes minimal.
> 
> Key decisions:
> - New artifact type `file` with fields: name, mime, size, text (extracted preview text optional? maybe `text` stored for agent) and no bytes in canvas.open.
> - Store bytes as BLOB in new table `file_content`.
> - Metadata stored in same table: name, mime. Extracted text in a separate `text` column capped 10k? For agent context, 10k per file is reasonable. Maybe allow 20k. Artifact text limit is 10k; use 10k for consistency.
> - New RPCs:
>   - `file.uploadBegin` {workspaceId, canvasId, expectedRevision, x,y,width,height, name, mime, size, text?} -> { uploadId, nodeId, artifactId } — but this commits? Staging.
>   - `file.uploadChunk` {workspaceId, uploadId, offset, dataBase64}
>   - `file.uploadFinish` {workspaceId, canvasId, uploadId, expectedRevision} -> {revision, node, artifact}
>   - `file.read` {workspaceId, artifactId} -> { data: base64, mime, name } — response can be big.
>   - `file.export`? Instead use opener.
> 
> Too many methods and staging complexity. Simpler chunked protocol:
> - `node.createFile`: metadata + first chunk? No.
> 
> Alternative: avoid backend staging by having frontend upload to a temp file in workspace data dir via Tauri command / HTTP endpoint, then a single `node.createFile` RPC references the uploadId. That's still staging.
> 
> Honestly, the simplest robust design: `node.createFile` accepts the entire file as base64, with a method-specific frame budget of 8 MiB. This avoids staging and multi-call complexity. Raise limits for this method only:
> - protocol: add `FILE_MAX_BYTES = 8*1024*1024`, `MAX_FILE_FRAME_BYTES = ~11 MB`.
> - runtime `handle_request`: parse method first? Currently checks bytes.len() > MAX_FRAME_BYTES before JSON parse. We can peek at the method by parsing JSON after size check but before rejecting: if bytes > MAX_FRAME_BYTES, do a light parse to check method == "node.createFile" and size <= MAX_FILE_FRAME_BYTES. That's reasonable. Same in `DesktopBackend::request` and HTTP body limit: HTTP reads with MAX_FRAME_BYTES; raise to MAX_FILE_FRAME_BYTES and let runtime enforce per-method. Also axum `max_buf_size(MAX_FRAME_BYTES)` is header buffer, not body — actually `max_buf_size` affects read/write buffer; leave.
> - `callRuntime` frontend: allow method-specific limit.
> - Tests asserting frame behavior need updates (tests/contracts/http). Let's check those asserts to plan.
> 
> Base64 8 MiB => 10.7 MB string; zod/base64 decode; SQLite blob 8 MB. Canvas.open excludes blob. File.read returns base64 of full file, 10.7 MB response. Hmm; image previews need bytes. Could instead stream via a URL? No HTTP in desktop. Use Tauri IPC response 10 MB okay-ish.
> 
> Maybe cap files at 4 MiB to keep memory sane (base64 5.4 MB). User might drop a 10 MB PDF; we can show clear error. Choose 8 MiB? Typical screenshots <2 MB; PDFs can be 5-10 MB. I'll use 8 MiB.
> 
> Wait, there is a much cleaner approach for previews and opening: store the file on disk under the workspace's data dir (`uploads/<artifactId>/<name>`) and add an RPC `file.read` for browser? Desktop could use `convertFileSrc` with asset protocol enabled. But asset protocol scope needs capabilities and CSP changes. Too much.
> 
> Stick with BLOB + base64 RPC.
> 
> - Extracted text: frontend extracts and sends with createFile (`text` field). For large files, sending base64 + text could exceed budget; cap text at 10k chars added ~10 KB, fine.
> 
> Rendering:
> - Images: fetch via `file.read`, create Blob URL, `<img>` with object-fit contain. Resize preserves aspect.
> - PDF: use `pdfjs-dist` to render first page or all pages? Preview node: render pages in a scrollable container at fitted width. Rendering requires worker. Use pdfjs. Add dependency. Node preview thumbnail can render page 1 only to keep it light; a full viewer maybe on "Read" button? The app has Modal/Reader. Simpler: render up to N pages lazily? Let's render page 1 as preview + page count and allow paging arrows. Good enough.
> - DOCX: use `mammoth` to extract HTML; render sanitized-ish inside a sandboxed iframe (no scripts). Legacy .doc: cannot parse; show metadata + note "Preview unavailable" and text placeholder. Agent text for .doc unavailable too. User explicitly chose DOCX plus legacy DOC; support import/preview fallback/open externally, no agent text. Hmm "Agent can read contents" for .doc won't work. Could use `word-extractor` npm for .doc? There's `word-extractor` package that parses .doc (binary Word 97) and .docx. Let me check availability and quality; it exists. But adding 4 deps (pdfjs-dist, mammoth, word-extractor) and bundling might be heavy. Alternatively, use `docx-preview` for rendering docx. Mammoth + DOMPurify? Mammoth output is safe-ish by design but should sanitize. Use a sandboxed iframe.
> 
> Maybe avoid mammoth: for docx, use JSZip to extract `word/document.xml` and strip tags manually? That's regex XML parsing — not great but simple and no heavy dependency; docx is a zip so need a zip lib. Mammoth is the standard; use it.
> 
> For .doc legacy, `word-extractor` adds a binary parser. Could accept .doc but only metadata/open externally. The user selected it, so at least store it. I'll note extraction limitations.
> 
> Text-like files: decode as UTF-8 and store text; preview as scrollable preformatted text/read-only markdown? Use Markdown component for .md (but only render local text; markdown.ts strips images). Simple <pre> preview is fine, maybe reuse TextNode-like display.

> - Rust method `file.open`? Runtime shouldn't open apps. In Tauri main.rs add command `open_file` that takes artifact ref, uses runtime `file.read` through a new public API? Commands::Runtime has `call` maybe private. Expose a helper on Runtime: `pub fn read_file_bytes(...) -> Result<Vec<u8>, RuntimeError>` then write temp + `tauri_plugin_opener::open_path`.
> - Adding plugin-opener: add Cargo dep `tauri-plugin-opener = "2"`, init plugin, capability `opener:allow-open-path`. Also need a temp dir. Use std::env::temp_dir + sanitized filename + artifact id subdir. Write bytes. Then opener open_path.
> - But `artifact_file` command needs `&mut Runtime` behind mutex; do it in spawn_blocking.
> 
> Browser mode: no system open; trigger download `<a download>`.
> 
> Alternatively skip plugin and use `std::process::Command` platform-specific. No — plugin is safer and standard.
> 
> Let me check tauri-plugin-opener version availability offline? Network may be available. Cargo build will download. Check Cargo.lock for opener. Probably absent. `pnpm add` for npm libs needs network. Let's test network/registry access before committing to dependencies. Also Rust crates may need network; environment may have cached registry.

> 1. `file.upload` — begin? Actually we can avoid server-side staging by uploading chunks to a temp artifact row linked to no node:

>    - `file.chunk` {workspaceId, uploadId, offset, data} appends; validates order, total ≤ size.
>    - `file.finish` {workspaceId, canvasId, expectedRevision, uploadId, x,y,width,height} → atomically verifies received=size, copies blob to file_content, creates artifact + node, bumps canvas revision, deletes upload.
>    - If abandoned, uploads linger. Clean up uploads older than e.g. 1 hour at begin, or when workspace closes. Simple: `DELETE FROM file_upload WHERE created_at < now-3600` on begin. Add created_at. Not perfect but fine.
>    - Need `file.read` {workspaceId, artifactId} → { data base64 }. For preview only.
>    - Delete: node.delete cleanup for file_content and uploads.

>    Chunk ordering: offset must equal previous received. Each chunk ≤ 8192 raw bytes (base64 10924 chars + JSON ~11.2 KB < 16 KiB). Frontend chunks sequentially, await each. For 8 MiB = 1024 requests. Could use 10,000 raw bytes? Base64 13,334 + JSON overhead (~200) = 13.5 KB, safe. 8 MiB => 839 requests. Use 9,000? Use 11,000 raw → 14,667 + 230 = 14,897. Safe. 8 MiB => 763 requests. Hmm.

import {
  CanvasOperationJsonSchema,
  type CanvasOperation,
  type RuntimeResult,
} from "@agentica/protocol";
import {
  CANVAS_AGENT_LIMITS,
  runCanvasAgentHarness,
  type CanvasAgentProgress,
  type HarnessMessage,
  type HarnessModel,
  type HarnessToolCall,
  type HarnessToolDefinition,
} from "./canvas-harness.ts";
import { checkedToolOperation, stageOperations } from "./canvas-agent.ts";
import {
  getRequestTimeoutMs,
  validateProvider,
  type ProviderConfig,
} from "./provider.ts";
import { isTauri } from "@tauri-apps/api/core";

export const DEFAULT_MODEL = "openrouter/free";
/** Provider prompts are not runtime frames; the 16 KiB RPC cap is too small. */
export const MAX_PROVIDER_REQUEST_BYTES = 256 * 1024;

const KEY_STORAGE = "agentica.openrouterApiKey";
const MODEL_STORAGE = "agentica.openrouterModel";

export function getOpenRouterApiKey(): string {
  try {
    const stored = localStorage.getItem(KEY_STORAGE);
    if (stored !== null && stored !== undefined) return stored.trim();
  } catch {
    // Storage may be unavailable
  }
  return (
    (typeof import.meta !== "undefined"
      ? (import.meta.env?.VITE_OPENROUTER_API_KEY as string | undefined)?.trim()
      : undefined) ?? ""
  );
}

export function setOpenRouterApiKey(key: string): void {
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(KEY_STORAGE, key.trim());
  } catch {
    // Storage may be unavailable
  }
}

export function getOpenRouterModel(): string {
  try {
    const stored = localStorage.getItem(MODEL_STORAGE);
    if (stored && stored.trim()) return stored.trim();
  } catch {
    // Storage may be unavailable
  }
  return (
    (typeof import.meta !== "undefined"
      ? (import.meta.env?.VITE_OPENROUTER_MODEL as string | undefined)?.trim()
      : undefined) || DEFAULT_MODEL
  );
}

export function setOpenRouterModel(model: string): void {
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(MODEL_STORAGE, model.trim() || DEFAULT_MODEL);
  } catch {
    // Storage may be unavailable
  }
}

export interface OpenRouterChatResponse {
  choices?: Array<{
    message?: {
      role?: string;
      content?: string;
    };
    finish_reason?: string;
  }>;
  error?: {
    message?: string;
    code?: number | string;
  };
}

function endpointHost(baseUrl: string): string {
  try {
    return new URL(baseUrl).host;
  } catch {
    return baseUrl;
  }
}

export async function canvasToolSupport(
  model: string,
  signal?: AbortSignal,
): Promise<boolean> {
  // The free router filters models by requested features, including tools.
  if (model === DEFAULT_MODEL) return true;
  const response = await fetch("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", {
    signal,
  });
  if (!response.ok)
    throw new Error(
      "Could not check the model's canvas tool support. Check your connection and retry.",
    );
  const catalog = (await response.json()) as {
    data?: { id: string; supported_parameters?: string[] }[];
  };
  const entry = catalog.data?.find((entry) => entry.id === model);
  if (!entry)
    throw new Error(
      "This model was not found in OpenRouter's catalog. Check the model in Settings.",
    );
  return entry.supported_parameters?.includes("tools") ?? false;
}

/** The one tool exposed to the model. Creation IDs are generated on apply. */
function canvasToolDefinition(): HarnessToolDefinition {
  const schema = structuredClone(CanvasOperationJsonSchema);
  delete schema.$schema;
  const variants = schema.oneOf;
  if (!variants)
    throw new Error("Canvas tool schema is missing its operations.");
  for (const variant of variants) {
    const properties = variant.properties;
    const discriminator = properties?.op;
    const op =
      discriminator && typeof discriminator === "object"
        ? discriminator.const
        : undefined;
    if (!properties || typeof op !== "string" || !variant.required)
      throw new Error("Invalid canvas tool schema.");
    const generated = op.startsWith("create")
      ? ["nodeId", "artifactId"]
      : op === "connect"
        ? ["edgeId"]
        : [];

import { LIMITS, MAX_FRAME_BYTES } from "@agentica/protocol";

/**
 * Transport-agnostic harness for the main canvas agent.
 *
 * The harness owns every budget and validation rule so a provider adapter can
 * only translate messages into a completion. Guard rails enforced here:
 * bounded provider requests, a total and per-response tool-call budget, a tool
 * allowlist, unique call IDs, bounded arguments and reply text, a per-request
 * timeout, cancellation, rejection feedback for repair, and an early stop when
 * the model repeats the same rejected edit.
 */

export interface CanvasAgentLimits {
  /** Provider round trips per turn, including the turn's final answer. */
  maxRequests: number;
  /** Canvas edits accepted or rejected across the whole turn. */
  maxToolCalls: number;
  /** Tool calls the model may request in one response. */
  maxToolCallsPerResponse: number;
  /** Bytes allowed in one tool-call argument payload. */
  maxToolArgumentBytes: number;
  /** Characters allowed in the final reply. */
  maxReplyChars: number;
  /** Characters of a rejected call echoed back to the model. */
  maxFeedbackChars: number;
  /** Identical rejected calls tolerated before the turn stops. */
  maxRepeatedRejections: number;
  /** Deadline for one provider request. */
  requestTimeoutMs: number;
}

export const CANVAS_AGENT_LIMITS: CanvasAgentLimits = {
  maxRequests: 8,
  maxToolCalls: 32,
  maxToolCallsPerResponse: 16,
  maxToolArgumentBytes: MAX_FRAME_BYTES,
  maxReplyChars: LIMITS.text,
  maxFeedbackChars: 500,
  maxRepeatedRejections: 3,
  requestTimeoutMs: 90_000,
};

/** Live counters shown while a turn generates. */
export interface CanvasAgentProgress {
  requests: number;
  maxRequests: number;
  stagedEdits: number;
  rejectedToolCalls: number;
  toolsEnabled: boolean;
}

/** One compact line for the composer, for example "Request 2 of 8 · 1 edit staged". */
export function agentProgressLabel(progress: CanvasAgentProgress): string {
  const request = `Request ${Math.min(progress.requests, progress.maxRequests)} of ${progress.maxRequests}`;
  if (!progress.toolsEnabled) return request;
  const edits = `${progress.stagedEdits} ${progress.stagedEdits === 1 ? "edit" : "edits"} staged`;
  const rejected = progress.rejectedToolCalls
    ? ` · ${progress.rejectedToolCalls} rejected`
    : "";
  return `${request} · ${edits}${rejected}`;
}

export type CanvasAgentGuardCode =
  | "INVALID_OUTPUT"
  | "REQUEST_LIMIT"
  | "TOOL_LIMIT"
  | "REPEATED_REJECTION"
  | "TIMEOUT";

/** A guard-rail failure. Provider and transport errors keep their own shapes. */
export class AgentGuardError extends Error {
  code: CanvasAgentGuardCode;

  constructor(code: CanvasAgentGuardCode, message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "AgentGuardError";
    this.code = code;
  }
}

export type HarnessRole = "system" | "user" | "assistant" | "tool";

export interface HarnessToolCall {
  id: string;
  type: "function";
  function: { name: string; arguments: string };
}

export interface HarnessMessage {
  role: HarnessRole;
  content: string | null;
  tool_calls?: HarnessToolCall[];
  tool_call_id?: string;
}

export interface HarnessToolDefinition {
  name: string;
  description: string;
  parameters: Record<string, unknown>;
}

export interface HarnessCompletion {
  content: string | null;
  toolCalls: HarnessToolCall[];
  finishReason?: string;
}

export interface HarnessRequestContext {
  messages: HarnessMessage[];
  /** The single allowed tool, or null when tools are disabled for this turn. */
  tool: HarnessToolDefinition | null;
  signal: AbortSignal;
}

/** Translate one request into a completion. Transport errors pass through. */
export type HarnessModel = (
  request: HarnessRequestContext,
) => Promise<HarnessCompletion>;
