use std::{env, fs, path::Path};

fn embed(path: &Path, url: &str, mime: &str, output: &mut String) {
    assert!(
        fs::symlink_metadata(path).unwrap().is_file(),
        "Assets must be regular files"
    );
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", path.display());
    output.push_str(&format!(
        "{url:?} => Some(({mime:?}, include_bytes!({:?}))),\n",
        path.canonicalize().unwrap()
    ));
}

fn main() {
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs");
    if env::var_os("CARGO_FEATURE_BUNDLED_FRONTEND").is_none() {
        return;
    }
    let dist = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../apps/desktop/dist");
    assert!(
        dist.join("index.html").is_file(),
        "Run pnpm --filter @agentica/desktop build first"
    );
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", dist.display());
    let mut output = String::from(
        "fn frontend_asset(path: &str) -> Option<(&'static str, &'static [u8])> { match path {\n",
    );
    embed(
        &dist.join("index.html"),
        "/",
        "text/html; charset=utf-8",
        &mut output,
    );
    embed(
        &dist.join("index.html"),
        "/index.html",
        "text/html; charset=utf-8",
        &mut output,
    );
    // shortcut: embed current Vite HTML/JS/CSS/fonts only; extend the allowlist when the UI adds assets.
    let assets = dist.join("assets");
    assert!(
        fs::symlink_metadata(&assets).unwrap().is_dir(),
        "Assets must be a directory"
    );
    let mut entries: Vec<_> = fs::read_dir(&assets)
        .unwrap()
        .map(|entry| entry.unwrap().path())
        .collect();
    entries.sort();
    for path in entries {
        let mime = match path.extension().and_then(|value| value.to_str()) {
            Some("js") => "text/javascript; charset=utf-8",
            Some("css") => "text/css; charset=utf-8",
            Some("woff") => "font/woff",
            Some("woff2") => "font/woff2",
            _ => continue,
        };
        let name = path.file_name().unwrap().to_str().unwrap();
        assert!(
            name.bytes()
                .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(byte, b'-' | b'_' | b'.')),
            "Unsupported asset name"
        );
        embed(&path, &format!("/assets/{name}"), mime, &mut output);
    }
    output.push_str("_ => None, } }\n");
    fs::write(
        Path::new(&env::var_os("OUT_DIR").unwrap()).join("frontend.rs"),
        output,
    )
    .unwrap();
}

> crc32

> external attrs 0
> local header offset
> name
> ```
> EOCD:
> ```
> sig 0x06054b50
> disk 0
> cd disk 0
> entries this disk
> total entries
> cd size
> cd offset
> comment len 0
> ```

> ```

# Initial architecture

The same frontend renders the canvas in Tauri or a local browser. Tauri links the
shared Rust runtime directly; the detached Axum executable runs independently of
browser tabs. The shared runtime owns domain validation and all SQLite
writes; transport and frontend code must not independently mutate application
tables. TypeScript wire contracts live in `packages/protocol`; the Rust handler
validates the same protocol, with integration tests checking compatibility.

## Current implementation

- The desktop host calls `DesktopBackend` through the scoped `runtime_request`
  command; application logic is linked into the same process.
- Detached mode exposes the same `Runtime::handle_request` through Axum over
  authenticated localhost HTTP; browser tabs share that runtime.
- The shared UI shows connection health, failures, and explicit reconnect.
- Protocol version 1 supports `runtime.ping` plus validated workspace, canvas,
  text-node, link, text-save, and layout-save commands. Invalid JSON or unsupported envelopes
  return an error with a null id; command errors are correlated and carry a
  stable code such as `WORKSPACE_LOCKED`, `CONFLICT`, or `STORAGE_ERROR`. Oversized desktop requests are rejected; HTTP rejects them
  with status 413. IDs use the same 128 UTF-16 code-unit limit in both languages.
- Requests are limited to 16 KiB. Browser health checks have a three-second
  deadline; HTTP headers, bodies, and runtime admission have five-second
  deadlines. Once admitted, persistence calls await their committed outcome.
- Each workspace is a directory holding an exclusive `writer.lock` and one
  SQLite database. Both modes take the lock before any write and reject a
  second writer, in either mode, with an actionable error.
- Canvas artifacts are text, drawings, or self-contained HTML designs. Designs
  are shown in a sandboxed frame with no scripts or remote resources; the
  runtime stores their source and never writes files into project folders.
- The local main window has only the runtime request capability; no file, shell,
  network, or database plugin permissions are exposed.

The shared UI does not yet use the persistence commands (M0-08). Managed files,
native PTY/preview operations, installers, and the Codex adapter are not
implemented. Cancellation, events, and version negotiation remain future work.
Concise implementation rationale belongs in [the changelog](../../CHANGELOG.md);
architecture decision files stay local and are not referenced or committed.

Open [the current application flow](application-flow.html) in a browser for an
interactive diagram of both launch modes, health-check responses, and lifecycle
behavior. Its editable source is [application-flow.architecture.json](application-flow.architecture.json).
The bundled viewer's attribution is in [third-party notices](../../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

## Next boundaries

Add `canvas-core`, `artifact-core`, `agent-core`, and `storage` packages when their
first implementations require those shared boundaries. Keep persistence owned by
the runtime, and keep authorization and revision checks on the mutation path.
Record concrete cross-component decisions and their rationale in the changelog.

The approved architecture and release requirements remain in
[PROJECT.md](../../PROJECT.md).

## Design references

[Dim0](https://github.com/vcmf/dim0) informs editable artifact interactions;
[ccanvas](https://github.com/DevoidSloth/ccanvas) informs coding-agent workflows;
[tldraw](https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw) informs spatial interaction patterns.
The selected implementation uses Svelte 5, Svelte Flow, and Tauri 2. Refer to

+function bytesToBase64(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
+  let binary = "";
+  for (let index = 0; index < bytes.length; index += 0x8000) {
+    binary += String.fromCharCode(...bytes.subarray(index, index + 0x8000));
+  }
+  return btoa(binary);
+}

+/// Write a copied canvas file to a temp path and open it with the system app.
+/// The filename is sanitized so artifact names cannot choose a directory.
+#[tauri::command]
+async fn open_file(
+    workspace_id: String,
+    artifact_id: String,
+    window: tauri::WebviewWindow,
+    state: tauri::State<'_, BackendState>,
+) -> Result<(), String> {
+    if window.label() != "main" {
+        return Err("File access is limited to the local main window.".into());
+    }
+    let backend = state.runtime.clone();
+    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
+        let (name, _mime, bytes) = backend
+            .lock()
+            .map_err(|_| "Backend state is unavailable.".to_owned())?
+            .file_bytes(&workspace_id, &artifact_id)
+            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join("agentica-files");
+        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+        let base = std::path::Path::new(&name)
+            .file_name()
+            .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
+            .unwrap_or("file");
+        let safe: String = base
+            .chars()
+            .map(|character| {
+                if character.is_control()
+                    || matches!(
+                        character,
+                        '<' | '>' | ':' | '"' | '/' | '\\' | '|' | '?' | '*'
+                    )
+                {
+                    '_'
+                } else {
+                    character
+                }
+            })
+            .collect();
+        let path = dir.join(format!("{artifact_id}-{safe}"));
+        std::fs::write(&path, bytes).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+        tauri_plugin_opener::open_path(&path, None::<&str>).map_err(|error| error.to_string())
+    })
+    .await
+    .map_err(|error| format!("File task failed: {error}"))?
+}

> _Reasoning_
> Potential issues found:
> - In editor.addFile, `document` captured before upload, and `this.load` with stale document. Busy prevents edits, but view changes (pan/zoom) might happen during upload? `panOnDrag={!isDrawingTool && !editorState.busy}` so busy blocks pan; zoomOnScroll blocked. Good.
> - If `file.finish` succeeds but `this.load` throws? unlikely.
> - `file.begin` text limit 10k, but `input.text` from extract is trimmed 10k; okay.
> - Editor addFile duplicates bytesToBase64 from file-types; could import from file-types (no runtime dep). file-types is safe for Node editor tests (no runtime import). We split precisely for that. Use `import { bytesToBase64 } from "./file-types";` in editor and remove local function; avoids duplication. Do it. Check Node test transform: file-types has only type import; safe.
> - Tauri open_file uses `_mime` unused but prefixed; okay.
> - `file.read` result `size` unbounded in schema but source validated; fine.
> - `FileMimeSchema` uses zod enum and frontend type; fine.
> - `file.chunk` regex requires full 4-char groups, base64 of 11,000 bytes = 14,668 chars (14,667? 11000/3*4 = 14666.67 -> padded), valid.
> - `FILE_LIMITS.chunkData` 15,000; 11k raw base64 14,668 < 15k.
> - `file.begin` requires canvas revision? It validates canvas exists but doesn't bump; fine. On finish canvas revision check. Upload can be staged even if canvas changes; finish conflicts and editor discards.
> - Rust `file.begin` allows zero-size; frontend handles.
> 
> Check the docx file mimetype normalization: browsers may report `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document` or empty; extension fallback. Good.
> - File `.md` reported `text/markdown` or empty; handled.
> - `.csv` reported `application/vnd.ms-excel` or `text/csv`? Browser usually text/csv; if application/vnd.ms-excel, extension fallback not reached because `MIME_BY_TYPE[type]` undefined → falls back to extension .csv → text/csv. Good.
> - `.svg` browser type image/svg+xml; good.
> - `.jpg` reported image/jpeg; mapped.
> 
> Check `FILE_ACCEPT` includes both `.jpg` and `.jpeg` and MIME strings. Fine.
> 
> Now the Rust commands diff to review for subtle SQL issues.

> _Reasoning_
> Looks fine. One bug: `file.finish` receives `text` (extracted at import) from `file_upload`; validated at begin. Good.
> 
> But `file.finish` deletes `file_upload` and relies on FK cascade for `file_chunk`. Foreign keys are on at runtime (`conn.pragma_update foreign_keys true` after open). Verified by test? File content deletion test doesn't check chunks; but file.read after delete works. Chunks would linger if FK off. PRAGMA is on. Could explicitly delete chunks before upload to be safe:
> ```rust
> tx.execute("DELETE FROM file_chunk WHERE upload_id = ?1", ...)?;
> ```
> before deleting upload. Not necessary but robust. Also `file.discard` relies on cascade. Add explicit delete in both for clarity. Do it.
> 
> Also `canvas.delete` cascade deletes uploads via FK, but orphan chunks cascade. Good. Add explicit in discard/finish.
> 
> Another concern: `file.begin` cleanup deletes stale uploads; cascades chunks. Good.
> 
> Add explicit chunk deletion.
